Writing the singleton indicator as the product of the coordinate factors shows that a distinct-index derivative survives exactly when every negative coordinate lies in the chosen index set, with magnitude \(2^{-k}\). Counting the surviving index sets at Hamming radius \(r\) gives the exact pointwise formula and, after shell counting, the exact \(L_p\) norm identity. Maximizing the exponent \(r+(k-r)p/2\) gives the three fixed-\(p\) regimes. Keeping \(p=2+\lambda/\log n\) in the same finite sum gives the displayed critical crossover. Most importantly, the primary source was read at Section 6.3: its Lemma 6.3 evaluates the same point as \((-2)^k\), whereas the direct calculation gives \((-1)^k2^{-k}\). The corrected \(r=k\) shell still yields growth of order \(n^{k/p}\), so the source exponent-sharpness conclusion survives although its normalization does not.
